next_step: Finalize committed capacity and sign SOW; legal review of DPA
notes:
Summary: Mid-market B2B SaaS (product analytics + personalization) evaluating Redwood Hosted -> Dedicated for production. Primary drivers: predictable unit economics for high-traffic personalization calls, lower p95 latency for in-product assistant, and stronger tenancy controls (VPC/KMS).

POC recap (4-week):
- Week 1: Hosted API quickstart, sample integration with feature flag. baseline latency 180-220ms P95 on hosted.
- Week 2: Dedicated demo environment spun up (dev pool). Engineered prompt prefix caching; P95 improved to 95-130ms for chat flows.
- Week 3: Throughput test for embeddings endpoint: target 300 embed/s, sustained ~220 embed/s without further tuning.
- Week 4: Regression evals on personalization reranking; quality delta minimal vs baseline model.

Pricing / packaging negotiation notes:
- Zenport wants committed capacity for Dedicated with burst window. Initial commercial ask: committed spend $15k/month (6-month ramp) with ability to burst up to 2.5x baseline for 2 hours/day peak.
- Redwood proposal v2 (attached): committed $20k/month for baseline (guaranteed capacity), 3-month ramp: 40% month1, 70% month2, 100% month3. Burst allowed at 1.8x baseline at 1.25x committed rate; true overage billed at 1.6x committed unit price beyond burst.
- Zenport counter: wants burst up to 2x at same committed unit-rate for first 6 months; also asks for credits if latency SLO not met for >3% of requests.
- Discussed annual vs monthly commitment. Prefers 12-month SOW but wants opt-out clause if product MAU < X (customer metric).

Technical / commercial constraints:
- SLOs: target p95 < 120ms for assistant chat in EU/NA; Redwood metrics show p95 ~100ms in Dedicated dev pool (good), but need SLA language for production.
- Security: must pass legal DPA and have SAML SSO + KMS key controls. Data residency: primary in NA, EU for EU customers.
- Integration: SAML + SCIM timeline uncertain (engineering estimate 6 weeks). That is a gating item for procurement.

Quotes / snippets from calls:
- "If we can get a predictable bill and reliable burst during launches, we can commit to the 12-month SOW." — Head of Product (A. Morgan)
- "Need explicit ramp schedule and a cap on overage dollars for Q1." — CFO (D. Patel)

Action items / next steps:
- AE (Maya) to push final pricing term sheet w/ Redwood legal by 2026-03-10.
- SE (Carlos) to send detailed perf runbook + P95 breakdown by region (due 2026-03-04).
- Legal: Zenport to send redlines on DPA (received 2026-02-28) — two major items: data deletion SLA, subprocessors list.
- Schedule procurement sync (30m) w/ CFO + Legal: target 2026-03-12.

Open questions / blockers (short):
- Exact burst pricing math: 1.6x vs 1.25x — need reconciliation.
- Contract clause for ramp failure / credits if Redwood misses ramped capacity.
- SAML + SCIM delivery date for SSO.

Internal notes (AE/SE):
- Competitive risk: OpenAI + ModelServeX pitching easier integration but no dedicated tenancy + higher unit costs at scale.
- Suggested concession: 2-month trial at 75% committed price or 10% on-boarding credit to offset initial ramp uncertainty.
- Keep negotiation focused on clear ramp milestones, capped overage dollars first quarter, and SLO credit language.
